title: Roos fibres preserve cones, shifts and levelwise quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $R$ a sheaf of rings on the pro-étale site $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use cochain complexes and cones of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a strict inverse tower $N=(N_n,t_n)_{n\ge1}$ of cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-inverse-system], let $P(N)=\prod_nN_n$ be the termwise product [def-weil-category-product], let $s_N=1-T_N$ with $\operatorname{pr}_nT_N=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$, and set $H(N)=\operatorname{Cone}(s_N)[-1]$. In reordered coordinates,
$$H(N)^q=P(N)^q\oplus P(N)^{q-1},\qquad d(v,u)=(dv,-du-s_Nv).$$
On strict tower maps let $H$ act diagonally by the product map. This is an additive functor, it sends levelwise quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms, and its localized Roos triangle makes $QH(N)$ a derived limit of $(QN_n)_n$ in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]. For every strict tower map $f:N\to N'$ there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$H(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(H(f)),\qquad(b,a,b',a')\mapsto(b,b',a,-a'),$$
in source order $P(N')^q,P(N)^{q+1},P(N')^{q-1},P(N)^q$. It preserves the cone inclusion and boundary after the shift comparison. The coherent natural shift comparison $H(N[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}H(N)[r]$ is $(v,u)\mapsto(v,(-1)^r u)$. If $j_n:M\to N_n$ are compatible chain maps, $m\mapsto((j_n(m))_n,0)$ is a natural chain map $M\to H(N)$. The cone and shift comparisons carry such zero-second-coordinate augmentations to the induced cone and shifted augmentations whenever the levelwise augmentations do so.

source.place: Cones paragraph, Roos-fibre sentence and cone/shift commutation sentence. Supporting sources: Stacks Tag 08TC (definition-derived-limit) and Tag 07KC (lemma-products).

proof.text: By [det-pe-products-derived], termwise products exist. The product universal property [def-weil-category-product] and the chain-map and strict-map equations [def-weil-inverse-system] give $dT_N=T_Nd$ and $P(f)s_N=s_{N'}P(f)$ after each projection. Products preserve identities, composition and addition by the same test. Apply [lem-pe-endomorphism-fibre-coordinate-calculus] to $(P(N),s_N)$. This gives exactly the displayed differential, additive diagonal functor and coherent shift comparison of the item, under the projection-preserving identifications $P(N[r])=P(N)[r]$.

source.place: Cones paragraph; assembly step 1 from the extracted endomorphism-fibre lemmas and the existing product and coordinate lemmas.

proof.text: For a levelwise quasi-isomorphism $f$, [det-pe-products-derived] makes $P(f)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-pe-roos-coordinates-quasi-iso] with $V=P(N)$, $V'=P(N')$, $L=H(N)$, $L'=H(N')$ and endomorphisms $-s_N,-s_{N'}$. Its differential $(dx,sx-dy)$ and diagonal map are precisely those given by step 1. Hence $H(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, without boundedness assumptions.

source.place: Cones paragraph; assembly step 2 from the extracted endomorphism-fibre lemmas and the existing product and coordinate lemmas.

proof.text: By [det-pe-products-derived], $QP(N)$ with its localized projections is the product of the $QN_n$. Consequently $Q(s_N)$ is their one-minus-transition map. The distinguished cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], inverse-rotated by TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], is $QH(N)\to QP(N)\xrightarrow{Q(s_N)}QP(N)\to QH(N)[1]$. Its maps are $(v,u)\mapsto v$ and $w\mapsto(0,w)$: inverse rotation cancels the minus sign in the cone boundary $-p$. This is a Roos triangle, so $QH(N)$ is a derived limit by [def-weil-derived-limit].

source.place: Cones paragraph; assembly step 3 from the extracted endomorphism-fibre lemmas and the existing product and coordinate lemmas.

proof.text: For $f:N\to N'$, the product projections identify $P(\operatorname{Cone}(f))$ with $\operatorname{Cone}(P(f))$: the inverse pairs the two coordinates at each level [def-weil-category-product]. Under this identification the endomorphism is $\operatorname{diag}(s_{N'},s_N)$. Apply [lem-pe-endomorphism-fibre-double-cone] with $A=P(N)$, $B=P(N')$, $s=s_N$, $t=s_{N'}$. It gives exactly the asserted four-coordinate isomorphism, its naturality, cone inclusion and boundary compatibility. Its $\sigma_1$ is the comparison of step 1.

source.place: Cones paragraph; assembly step 4 from the extracted endomorphism-fibre lemmas and the existing product and coordinate lemmas.

proof.text: For compatible $j_n$ let $J=(j_n)_n:M\to P(N)$. Projectionwise $s_NJ=0$, and a compatible augmented square gives $P(f)J=J'g$ [def-weil-category-product, def-weil-inverse-system]. The augmentation and shift identities of [lem-pe-endomorphism-fibre-coordinate-calculus] give the asserted natural map $(J,0)$ and shifted compatibility. The cone augmentation identity of [lem-pe-endomorphism-fibre-double-cone], using the product/cone identification of step 4, gives the final cone compatibility.

source.place: Cones paragraph; assembly step 5 from the extracted endomorphism-fibre lemmas and the existing product and coordinate lemmas.

lean.statement: theorem roos_cone_calculus (X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}) (R : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt.topology X) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R)] : (roosF (A := ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R)).Additive ∧ CoordinateCalculus (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ∧ (∀ {N N' : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ} (f : N ⟶ N'), (∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso ((HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex.map f).app (op n))) → QuasiIso (roosF.map f)) ∧ (∀ N : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ, DerivedRoos N) ∧ ∃ (cs : (roosF (A := ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R)).CommShift ℤ) (e : ∀ {N N' : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ} (f : N ⟶ N'), roosF.obj (mappingCone f) ≅ mappingCone (roosF.map f)) (hnat : AugmentationNaturality (ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R)), ShiftFormula cs ∧ (∀ {N N' : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max u (t + 1)} R) ℤ} (f : N ⟶ N'), ConeFormula f (e f)) ∧ ConeCompatibility cs e ∧ ConeAugmentation e hnat ∧ ShiftAugmentation cs
